# ERF workspace map

Loaded automatically when a session reads anything under this folder. It says what each
part of the folder is for and how work here runs. Business facts are NOT here - they
live in `CONTEXT.md`. Open decisions and entry status live in `PROJECT-PLAN.md`.

## Read first, by task

| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| Anything about the business (prices, contacts, access, NAP) | `CONTEXT.md` |
| Any live-site edit | `../../portal/SQUARESPACE-REFERENCE.md`, then `PROJECT-PLAN.md` "Decisions already taken" |
| Design judgement on the Squarespace site | `../../playbooks/squarespace-polish.md` (its Scope section: ERF is being replaced by a custom build, so polish spend is throwaway) |
| The custom rebuild | `rebuild/PROJECT-PLAN.md` |
| SEO / AEO on-page work | `seo-onpage/PROJECT-PLAN.md` |

## The live site is the source of truth

The site is Squarespace 7.1 Basic, edited by browser automation against the live admin.
There is no local build and no PR for a live edit. Every `*-payload.html`, `*-LIVE*.html`
and `.less` file in this folder is a **snapshot**, not the current state. Before editing,
pull the live block or the compiled `custom.css` and work from that.

## How a live change runs

Each change gets its own folder, `<topic>-<YYYY-MM-DD>/`, with numbered scripts in run
order. Examples: `contact-copy-2026-09-21/` and `meta-descriptions-2026-09-20/`.

1. **Probe**: `01-*.mjs` reads the live page or editor state. Save what you pulled
   (`live-*.html`, `custom-css-before.less`) as the restore point.
2. **Payload**: the new HTML or CSS, saved in the folder.
3. **Apply**: the script that writes it. Rich text uses TipTap `setContent`, never
   `innerHTML` or paste. Check the block content before clicking SAVE.
4. **Verify from outside**: an anonymous fetch (`*verify-anon.mjs` or plain `curl`), then
   screenshots at 1440 and 390. The admin session lies about what is public.
5. **Log**: `node ~/.claude/scripts/change-log.js` with project `engineroomfitness`,
   and update the entry's row in `PROJECT-PLAN.md`.

A folder with a payload and no anonymous verify has not shipped. Treat it as unfinished.

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `squarespace/` | Custom CSS backups and restore points (`css-restore/`), per-section `.less` |
| `hero-recovery-2026-09-20/` | Most recent custom CSS snapshots (`custom-css-live-2026-09-21.less`) |
| `home-restructure/`, `our-classes-*`, `contact-copy-*`, `about-us-*`, `footer-rebuild/`, `coaches-squarespace/`, `gym-news-cards/`, `open-day-*`, `pricing-visibility/`, `reviews/` | One folder per page or section change: scripts, payloads, live snapshots |
| `meta-descriptions-2026-09-20/`, `seo-onpage/`, `gsc-reindex/`, `psi/` | SEO, indexing and speed work |
| `gbp-video-2026-09-21/` | Google Business Profile automation |
| `hero-triptych/`, `home1-hero-video/` | Hero video builds (Python compositing) and the swap onto the live page |
| `assets/`, `logo*/`, `mockups/`, `before-rebuild/` | Images: before/after sets, headshots, logo work, mockups |
| `rebuild/` | Custom-build IA, content inventory, briefs |
| `reports/` | Client-facing reports. `sent/` holds what actually went to Eoin |
| `inbox/` | Material received from the client, as received |
| `phone-project/` | Instructions and knowledge for the claude.ai Project used for quick ERF SEO/AEO jobs from the phone |
| `drive-media-assessment/`, `checklist-2026-08-25/`, `style-parity-2026-08-25/` | Finished one-off assessments, kept for evidence |

Loose files at the root are dated briefs, drafts to Eoin, audits and design reviews.
Use the date in the filename to find the latest; the newest `DESIGN-REVIEW-*` and
`SITE-SCAN-*` are the current audit baseline.

## Where new work goes

- A new live change: a new `<topic>-<date>/` folder, laid out as above. Do not add
  scripts to an older change folder.
- A new client-facing report: `reports/`, then move it to `reports/sent/` once sent.
- Something Eoin sent: `inbox/`, unmodified.
- A new fact about the business: `CONTEXT.md`, in the same commit as the decision.

It serves existing 4 Squarespace clients, Engine Room Fitness included, and the audit, SEO, AI-visibility and 5 Google-reviews work that continues on clients' Squarespace sites. What retired on that date 6 is selling an in-platform visual upgrade to a NEW client, on Squarespace or any other 7 builder: a prospect on a builder is offered a custom Astro or Next.js build instead. Nothing here is an offer, and nothing here 8 is deprecated. See `docs/playbooks/builder-polish-capability.md`. 9 10 A living map of the Squarespace admin for client sites, so we don't re-discover the 11 IA every session. Squarespace renamed and reorganised its settings (the old 12 `Settings -> Advanced` no longer exists), and several client guides still point at 13 dead paths - this file is the corrected source. 14 15 **This file is the mechanics half.** For the design-quality half - what to change to 16 make an inherited Squarespace site stop looking cheap, in what order, and what a 17 prospect audit should name - see 18 [`docs/playbooks/squarespace-polish.md`](../playbooks/squarespace-polish.md). Keep the 19 two apart: platform behaviour and per-client change log here, reusable design judgement 20 there. 21 22 Current subject: **Handyman Clonakilty** (7.1, Basic plan). Always add the URL Mapping. - The admin preview iframe shows the live site; verify real changes against `https:///...` with curl (status + redirect), not just the preview. - CodeMirror fields (URL Mappings, Code Injection) resist synthetic clicks; use the CodeMirror API to set values. - Async-rendered panels: read AFTER they settle, not on first paint (a half-loaded Billing/Analytics panel shows blanks/zeros that look like real data). ## Automating the 7.1 gallery editor (browser-driven edits) 7.1's Gallery block ("GRID") is built on a legacy **YUI3 widget** (`yui3-widget sqs-content-item-image ...`), not the newer React-ish editors used elsewhere in the admin. It behaves differently from everything else in this doc: - **Simple clicks and CSS `:hover` overlays do not work here.** A trusted CDP click on the gallery block itself (selecting it, revealing the pencil "Edit" toolbar) DOES work fine - that part is normal. But once inside the block's "Upload Media" thumbnail grid, the individual thumbnails are **not in the accessibility tree at all** (no role, no alt, nothing to target by uid), and hover-only affordances need genuine cursor movement that a scripted `hover`/`click` call doesn't reproduce. Earlier attempts at this (recorded in a prior session's work order) concluded the whole thing "resists automation" and recommended doing it by hand. That conclusion was half right: single clicks and CSS-hover tricks really don't work. A **synthetic double-click**, dispatched directly at the DOM node, does: ```js const img = [...document.querySelectorAll('img')].find(i => i.src.includes(UNIQUE_ID)); const target = img.closest('.sqs-content-item-image'); const rect = target.getBoundingClientRect(); const opts = { bubbles:true, cancelable:true, clientX: rect.left+rect.width/2, clientY: rect.top+rect.height/2, view:window, button:0, buttons:1, pointerId:1, pointerType:'mouse', isPrimary:true, composed:true }; for (const t of ['pointerover','pointerenter','pointerdown','mousedown', 'pointerup','mouseup','click']) { const Ctor = t.startsWith('pointer') ? PointerEvent : MouseEvent; target.dispatchEvent(new Ctor(t, opts)); } target.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('dblclick', opts)); ``` This opens the real "EDIT IMAGE" dialog (Title / Body / Clickthrough URL), which IS a normal ``/`

**Plan only, nothing run, no browser opened.** It follows `docs/clients/engineroomfitness/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/portal/SQUARESPACE-REFERENCE.md`, whose sections I read down to line 947 of 3,567.

**Two things first**
- **Copy:** the new wording needs your sign-off. Your standing rule is no new display copy without you, so step 2 puts options to you before any edit.
- **Hero type:** "hero text" can be three different things on ERF. The homepage hero has been a poster-art Image Block and a hero-video triptych (`hero-triptych/`, `home1-hero-video/`). On those the text is baked into the image or video, so it is not editable text. I'd confirm which type the page has before anything else.

**Steps**

1. **Pick the page and classify its hero.**
   - Read the page's row in `PROJECT-PLAN.md` ("Decisions already taken") and the latest `DESIGN-REVIEW-*` for it.
   - Check what the first section holds. Entry 4 found several pages have no hero at all.
   - *Verify:* an anonymous `curl` of the live page shows the text in the HTML as an `<h1>` or `<h2>`, in a Code Block, or not at all.
     - If it's not in the HTML, the text is baked into an image and the job is an image swap, not a text edit.
     - If it's in a Code Block, edit the block source.
     - If it's a TipTap text block, use the steps below.

2. **Get approved wording from you.**
   - I put 2–3 options to you via `AskUserQuestion` and run the paraphrase and label tests on each.
   - *Verify:* you pick one. Liking an option isn't picking it.

3. **Prove access.**
   - Check the admin session is alive from the human's side. It expires silently to `login.squarespace.com`, and re-login is yours, not mine.
   - *Verify:* after navigating to `/config/pages`, `page.url()` is not `login.squarespace.com`.

4. **Probe and save a restore point.**
   - Create `hero-text-<page>-2026-10-12/` with `01-probe.mjs`.
   - Pull the live block HTML into `live-before.html`.
   - *Verify:* the file is non-empty and matches the anonymous fetch from step 1.

5. **Write the payload.**
   - Take the live block's exact `class`, `style` and `data-rte-preserve-empty` attributes and change only the text.
   - *Verify:* a diff of the payload against `live-before.html` shows only the wording changed.

6. **Open the page in the full editor canvas** (Edit, not the narrow Pages preview).
   - Select the block and don't hover near the header. Hovering there can trigger "Editing Site Header" and discard unsaved edits.
   - *Verify:* the toolbar badge shows the page and `Page · Published`, not "Editing Site Header".

7. **Apply with TipTap `setContent`.**
   - Use `element.editor.commands.setContent(html, true)`. Never `innerHTML`, never paste, and never `Ctrl+A` then `Backspace` on a one-line heading, which deletes the block.
   - *Verify:* before clicking SAVE, a guard asserts that:
     - the heading equals the new text,
     - the old-copy signature no longer appears,
     - the block count is unchanged.
   - If the guard fails, I don't save and I navigate away to discard.

8. **Save** with `[data-test="frameToolbarSave"]`.
   - *Verify:* the SAVE button greys out and the badge is unchanged.

9. **Verify from outside the admin session.**
   - Run an anonymous `curl` with a Chrome user agent, or a fresh cookie-less browser context.
   - *Verify:* the new text is in the raw HTML and the old text is gone. There is exactly one `<h1>`, and the status is 200. An admin-session fetch proves nothing here.

10. **Look at it.**
    - Take screenshots at 1440 and 390 and read both myself.
    - *Verify:* no mid-word break, no overlap with the offer strip or header, and no horizontal overflow at 768–999px, where header and hero overlap was fixed before.

11. **Log it.**
    - Run `change-log.js --project engineroomfitness` with the before and after wording and the restore-point folder.
    - Update the entry row in `PROJECT-PLAN.md`.
    - *Verify:* `change-log.js --list --project engineroomfitness` shows the new entry.

**Failure paths**
- If the guard in step 7 fails twice, I stop and report the assumption I'm least sure of.
- If the hero turns out to be image or video art, I stop at step 1 and come back with an image-swap plan. That plan has its own pitfalls: Replace wipes the alt text, and the CDN re-encodes below-native widths.
